## N-QUERY vs. C-FIND in DICOM

Both services are part of DIMSE (DICOM Message Service Element) and serve a query/lookup role, but they operate on fundamentally different data models:

### N-QUERY
- **Normalized service**: It operates on *normalized SOP Classes* — information objects that represent real-world entities (e.g., Patient, Study) directly, independent of any specific composite image/object.
- It queries normalized attributes of these managed entities using the normalized query/retrieve information model (e.g., Patient/Root Query/Retrieve models).
- Retrieval of the results requires the companion normalized services **N-RETRIEVE** and **N-MOVE**.
- N-QUERY/N-RETRIEVE were part of the original "normalized query/retrieve" model and were **retired/deprecated** in later DICOM versions because they were never widely adopted.

### C-FIND
- **Composite service**: It operates on *composite information objects* (e.g., images) and queries using composite attributes, following the hierarchical Patient–Study–Series–Instance information model.
- It is part of the widely used **C-based Query/Retrieve service class**, where matching results (identifiers) are returned, and actual object retrieval is done with **C-MOVE** or **C-GET**.
- C-FIND is the standard, universally implemented way to query modalities, PACS, and workstations.

### Key distinction
| Aspect | N-QUERY | C-FIND |
|---|---|---|
| SOP class type | Normalized | Composite |
| Information model | Normalized (entity-based) | Patient/Study-Root composite hierarchy |
| Companion retrieval | N-RETRIEVE / N-MOVE | C-MOVE / C-GET |
| Status | Retired/rarely used | Standard, ubiquitous |

In practice, C-FIND won out because the composite model mapped more naturally onto the actual stored objects, while the normalized model proved too complex to implement.
